family.tagline: Long interviews, quick spreadsheets, and one quiet shelf.
family.story: Obinna produces a podcast from the Desk Hall. Rhiannon, a data analyst, works at the next desk. Guests record in the house, and their raw files stay on the Core.

companion.name: Cass
companion.job: Opens AudioMass in its own browser and loads the latest interview file.
companion.limits: Loads a copy. Obinna does every edit.

companion.name: Gwen
companion.job: Finds the sheet or note Rhiannon asks for, from what she put in Companion Memory.
companion.limits: Finds and reports. Rhiannon opens and decides.

popup.title: A parcel, mid-edit
popup.body: The parcel arrives while Obinna is mid-edit. He carries it through the entry to the Desk Hall, and Rhiannon clears a space on the desk.

popup.title: Checking the packing list
popup.body: Rhiannon checks the list: the Companion Core, a power cable, a quick-start guide and a recovery USB drive. The footprint is about three quarters of a sheet of paper.

popup.title: Plug it in, then listen
popup.body: Obinna plugs in the cable and presses the button. The Core wakes and opens its own Wi-Fi network. At idle, it sits at nineteen decibels.

popup.title: Join it from the phone
popup.body: Rhiannon opens the Wi-Fi settings and joins the Core's own network. Then she picks the home network from the list.

popup.title: Pick your first agents and apps
popup.body: In Companion Hub, Obinna picks OpenClaw. Rhiannon picks Hermes and Companion Memory (beta). They add AudioMass, Nextcloud, Grist and Home Assistant, then walk away.

beats.capability: talks to you through the messaging platform you pick

popup.title: Gwen says hello
popup.body: Rhiannon messages the agent she named Gwen. Gwen answers, and the Core is running.
popup.note: Messages pass through the chat service you choose.

say.speaker: rhiannon
say.text: Hello, Rhiannon. Gwen here. Ready when you are.

beats.capability: edit audio in a browser tab: cut, fade, normalise, export

popup.title: Cass loads yesterday's interview
popup.body: Obinna asks Cass for yesterday's interview. Cass opens AudioMass in its own browser and loads a copy. Obinna makes every cut himself.

say.speaker: obinna
say.text: Copy loaded. The edit is yours.

beats.capability: your files, calendar and contacts on your own Core, synced to your devices

popup.title: One folder per guest
popup.body: Each guest gets a folder in Nextcloud on the Core. The raw takes live there, and the studio laptop syncs the same folder.

beats.capability: fill and sign PDF forms on any device, from your own Core

popup.title: The release form, signed here
popup.body: A guest fills and signs the release form on a tablet in the Desk Hall. Docuseal runs on the Core.

beats.capability: keep customers, deals and custom fields in a CRM you host yourself

popup.title: A sponsor, tracked as a deal
popup.body: A sponsor asks about the autumn run. Obinna adds the deal to Twenty with the dates and the notes from the call.

beats.capability: back up your files with encryption before they leave your Core

popup.title: Guest folders, copied to a disk
popup.body: Obinna points Duplicati at a local disk and backs up the guest folders. The copy sits in a drawer, a few steps from the Core.

beats.capability: a spreadsheet-database with real Python formulas, stored as a SQLite file you can copy

popup.title: Episodes and guests, one table
popup.body: Rhiannon keeps the episode schedule and guest list in one Grist table. Python formulas work out the dates, and the file is a SQLite file she can copy.

beats.capability: plan your day, track time and run a Pomodoro timer

popup.title: A workday in timed blocks
popup.body: Rhiannon plans her workday in Super Productivity and starts a Pomodoro timer for each block. The plan sits on the Core.

beats.capability: talks to you through the messaging platform you pick

popup.title: Gwen finds the forecast sheet
popup.body: Rhiannon asks Gwen where the March sheet went. Gwen finds it from what Rhiannon put into Companion Memory. Rhiannon opens it herself.

say.speaker: rhiannon
say.text: Found it. Please open the file to check.

beats.capability: write a wiki or a set of manuals in books, chapters and pages, with search and history

popup.title: The show handbook, written down
popup.body: Rhiannon writes the show handbook in BookStack: the guest briefing, the microphone checklist and the release steps.

beats.capability: stream your own music from your Core to a browser or an app

popup.title: After the export, the couch
popup.body: After the last export, Obinna stretches out on the couch and plays tonight's mix from mStream. It streams from the Core to his phone.

beats.capability: control and automate your smart home from one place, locally

popup.title: A lamp that says recording
popup.body: From the couch, Rhiannon adds the Desk Hall lamp to Home Assistant. One tap turns it red when Obinna records.

beats.capability: track the pantry, shopping lists, recipes, chores and household habits in one place

popup.title: The pantry, tracked at the bar
popup.body: Rhiannon tracks the pantry in Grocy at the breakfast bar. Obinna adds to the shopping list from his phone.

beats.capability: archive the receipts, warranties and contracts you rarely look at, until you need them

popup.title: A microphone receipt, filed
popup.body: Obinna scans the new microphone's receipt and warranty card into Papra at the counter. Both wait there until the day he needs them.

beats.capability: track the films, shows, books and games you have watched, read and played

popup.title: The reading list, kept in bed
popup.body: In bed, Rhiannon logs the novel she just finished in Yamtrack. Her reading list builds up on the Core, one title at a time.

beats.capability: track runs, rides and gear and see your fitness stats on your own server

popup.title: This morning's run, logged
popup.body: Rhiannon loads this morning's run into Endurain from a GPX file. The route and her shoe mileage sit on the Core.

beats.capability: edit multi-track video in your browser

popup.title: A trailer cut on the deck
popup.body: On the deck, Obinna cuts a trailer in FreeCut, using clips from the guest folders.

popup.title: Two desks, one quiet shelf
popup.body: A producer and an analyst share one Desk Hall. The Okonkwo-Reid household runs on one Companion Core, and the guests' recordings stay at home.

closing.body: Your recordings, your spreadsheets and your lamps can run from a Companion Core at home. Start with one guest folder in Nextcloud.

notes: Owner sign-off open: the FTUE hotspot flow is written as the owner specified and is not on the fact sheet (STORY-BIBLE section 15, item 1).
The Core stands on a desk in the Desk Hall (casting roles list no desk item, so hall beats anchor on the core or on room:office). The dining room has no camera eye, so no beat anchors there.
Whisper-WebUI and Metabase (casting signature apps) have no QA screenshot and are not on the reviewed list, so they are not used. Signature apps used: AudioMass, Nextcloud, Home Assistant.
ftue-plug-in: "nineteen decibels" is the sheet's 19 dB at idle [V]; the text says "At idle". Check the voice-over reads it naturally.
hall-release: Docuseal, never called legally binding (catalog caveat). Signers outside the home network need access to the Core, so the guest signs on a tablet in the house.
hall-backup: Duplicati names a local disk (catalog caveat). deck-trailer: FreeCut runs in the browser of the device that edits; no claim about where media goes.
deck-run: Endurain is logging only, no health outcome; Strava sync is off the table (outside service), GPX upload is local.

Voice-over lexicon: Okonkwo, Obinna, Rhiannon, Cass, Gwen, Loblolly, Docuseal, Duplicati, Grist, Grocy, Papra, BookStack, Endurain, FreeCut, AudioMass, Navidrome. Street and town are invented; the human map check is still open.
